findings.evidence: Code lines 205 and 208 hard-code order `1`; roadmap lines 102-104 and README lines 182-185 say condition (A′) is with a prescribed pole order, and HW Thm 3.3 condition (A) states flat of order `n` for a pole of order `n`.
findings.fix: Make condition (A′) order-aware, e.g. parameterize it by `f`/pole orders or prescribed order data, and require `FlatOfOrder ... n` for each pole of order `n` on the curve; do not present order-1 transversality as the full HW condition for higher-order poles.
findings.issue: `ConditionAprime` only requires `FlatOfOrder γ t₀ 1` and `FlatOfOrderBasepoint γ a b 1`, but HW condition (A) requires flatness of order equal to the on-curve pole order for higher-order poles; condition (B) only handles Laurent sector cancellation, so this loses a necessary PV-existence hypothesis.

findings.evidence: Code lines 182-193 use `‖γ t - (γ t₀ + (t - t₀) • t_plus)‖`; HW Def. 3.2 defines `|Γ(x)-P±(Γ(x))| = o(|Γ(x)-z₁|^n)` with `P±` the orthogonal projection to the tangent lines.
findings.fix: Define flatness using the geometric distance from `γ t` to the appropriate tangent line/projection, and apply the same correction to the basepoint version.
findings.issue: `FlatOfOrder`/`FlatOfOrderBasepoint` measure distance to the parametrized affine approximation `γ t₀ + (t-t₀) • v`, not distance to the orthogonal projection onto the tangent line as in HW Def. 3.2; for example a curve lying on its tangent line with nonlinear speed is geometrically flat of every order but fails this definition for high orders.

summary: The new condition (A′) is not faithful to HW’s higher-order hypothesis, and the exported flatness predicate does not match the paper’s geometric definition for orders above 1.
